Limits: All 81 commands returned exactly their requested Q and D nodes with finite delay. This is independent path-query evidence supplementing the previous report, whose detailed-path limit showed only 26 internal links.

The official installed command guide specifies default slow/max. Four native slow/max Q-to-D values available in the scoped RTR exactly match these queries. The 45 comparisons against fast and/or min are intentionally different analysis modes and their differences are not errors.

The tool logs coarse delay table initialization. That initialization alone does not establish that the final returned routed-path delays use a coarse estimate. The like-for-like native slow/max agreement supports the four directly comparable paths; it does not separately calibrate every other returned value.

The maximum 0.636ns is the returned slow/max Q-to-D path delay, not an external measurement or full STA slack. Starting at Q excludes clock-to-Q; ending at D excludes destination setup/hold, clock skew/uncertainty, and metastability MTBF.
This query does not prove all 81 links under both corners and both min/max analyses. The prior scoped STA review remains unchanged; no broad claim of complete physical CDC signoff is made.

The six previously ignored PAP_ASYNC_REG mapping attributes are preserved as prior warnings; each associated Q-to-D query returned its exact path. They are not six warnings from this query execution, and successful path queries do not retroactively make ignored attributes effective.
